newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Opposition jets bomb Kabul airport, no casualties.
newsitem.headline: Opposition jets bomb Kabul airport, no casualties.

text.p: Opposition warplanes dropped a bomb on Kabul airport on Sunday but caused no casualties or damage, officials of the Taleban Islamic militia said.
Aid workers in the opposition-held northern city of Mazar-i-Sharif retracted earlier reports that Taleban jets had dropped two bombs there in the early hours.
U.N. officials said an accidental grenade explosion at the city's Balkh University had created rumours of an air raid.
A Kandahar-based Taleban spokesman, Mohammad Haqqani, said he knew of no raids by the militia's air force on Sunday.
Taleban officials in Kabul said one bomb had hit the airport, in a northeastern district of the city, in the dawn air raid. There were no casualties and no damage to the runway.
Residents awoke to a deafening anti-aircraft barrage as Taleban gunners fired on two jets flying high over the city.

Taleban forces fought through the night in the vicinity of Jabal os-Siraj, a strategic town about 70 km (45 miles) north of Kabul, gaining more ground, according to the Pakistan-based Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) news service.
AIP said the Taleban had killed at least 27 fighters loyal to former government military chief Ahmad Shah Masood and captured 80. Four Taleban were killed and several wounded.
It said the fighting had put the Taleban in control of an area containing five villages east of the Salang highway.
Masood controls the Salang Pass north of Jabal os-Siraj, as well as his native Panjsher Valley northeast of the town.
Sunday's raid on Kabul followed one on Friday night when an opposition jet dropped two bombs on the airport. One landed in the air defence section, killing at least one Taleban fighter.
Taleban officials said there was no damage to the runway at the airport, which is used by military and civilian aircraft.

Friday's air strike appeared to be retaliation for last week's Taleban bombing raids on Maimana, capital of the northeastern province of Faryab, held by forces loyal to northern opposition leader General Abdul Malik.
A spokesman for Malik, General Humayun Fauzi, said on Friday that Taleban raids had killed 90 people in Maimana within 48 hours, including 40 Taleban prisoners.
Fauzi said two Taleban officials, Foreign Minister Mullah Mohammad Ghous and Civil Aviation Minister Maulvi Akhter Mohammad Mansoor were among 30 wounded in the bombing.

But an independent military source said there had been no casualties in the raids on Maimana, which Taleban officials have said was in reprisal for earlier opposition air strikes on the Taleban-held city of Kunduz in northeastern Afghanistan.
The Taleban, who captured Kabul in September, are fighting to impose their strict Islamic rule across Afghanistan, but have failed to quell opposition forces in the north.
